Reading Text

ملخص القراءة
Reading Passage · نص القراءة
You Look Just Like Me!
أنت تشبهني تمامًا!
🔊 MP3-Synced Reading 00:00 / 00:00
Speed: 1.0×
🛠 Fix Sync — Adjust Highlight Timing استمع للصوت واضغط 🎯 عند بداية كل جملة، أو استخدم +/- للضبط الدقيق
👆 Touch or hover any word to see its Arabic translation instantly.  |  المسّ أي كلمة لترى ترجمتها فوراً

This is the story of an amazing coincidence. Bobby Shafran started a new semester at a college in New York. Strangely, other students kept calling him Eddy – a student who had studied there the semester before. Bobby and Eddy had never met, but they looked exactly alike.

Another student confused Bobby with Eddy, and then realised they were probably brothers, and introduced them to each other. Bobby and Eddy soon found out that they were, in fact, twins – born at the same time, but raised as orphans in two different families. Neither family knew their baby boy had a brother.

The story became even more amazing. After it appeared in the newspapers, another boy named David Kellman saw it and realised that he, too, was their brother – also born at the same time. So the twins became triplets!

Another well-known story is that of Daphne Goodship and Barbara Herbert. They met for the first time at the age of 39, yet they had many things in common. Each was wearing a beige dress and a brown jacket. They both liked their coffee cold, and blue was their favourite colour. Because they laughed so much and had similar personalities, scientists called them the "Giggle twins."

Scientists find such stories touching. They study twins and triplets to learn about heredity and environment – and why some people grow up so similar, even when they never met.
